newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit remains weak, seen testing recent lows.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit remains weak, seen testing recent lows.

text.p: * Ringgit remains weak on firm dollar sentiment and unexpectedly large June trade deficit
* Market watching for possible central bank intervention at 2.6500
The ringgit remained weak in early Asian trading although its fall was limited by dollar sales by local corporates, dealers said.
At 0230 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.6405/35 to a dollar after hitting a low of 2.6445. It closed at 2.6340/70 in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday.
"The dollar trend is still strong. The swaps restriction will not be effective for a while as the market is well funded," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
He said the market was already long on ringgit positions and offshore players accounted for the bulk of liquidity in the forward market.
"That's why swaps rates were not affected," he said.
Dealers said there was talk in the market that Bank Negara was checking on local banks this morning, trying to gauge the extent of the recent capital control measure.
Bank Negara announced on Sunday that local banks would have to limit their non-trade related currency swaps to $2.0 million with each overseas customer, from Monday.
The curbs are part of an effort to cool speculation in the ringgit and to bring down interest rates.
Dealers said ringgit sentiment continued to be affected by an unexpectedly large trade deficit of 2.8 billion ringgit for June after a surplus of 156.2 million in May.

Some local corporates were seen selling dollar/ringgit around 2.6440 in early trade but the rebound was limited by talk of good-sized bids for dollar/ringgit at 2.6400 from local and offshore players.

Dealers said given its bullish sentiment, the dollar was on track to retest its recent high of 2.6530 against the ringgit. But the market will be watching for possible central bank intervention at the 2.6500 level, they said.
